雒于仁〔貫陝西西安府三原縣民籍，涇陽縣人，國子生，治《書經》，字依仲，行一，年三十四，五月初四日生〕。曾祖維〔壽官〕；祖昂〔累贈太常寺少卿〕；父遵〔光祿寺卿〕；母李氏〔封孺人，累贈恭人〕，繼母張氏〔累封恭人〕。具慶下。弟于翰〔監生〕。娶段氏。陝西鄉試第二十一名，會試第二百五十五名。

賈尚志〔貫河南南陽府南陽縣民籍，縣學生，治《書經》，字士事，行四，年二十九，六月十六日生〕。曾祖洪；祖祿；父鎮；母張氏。具慶下。弟尚友。娶潘氏。河南鄉試第六十八名，會試第二百二十八名。

田勸〔貫河南潁川衛官籍，直隸潁州人，國子生，治《詩經》，字作民，行三，年三十二，六月初五日生〕。曾祖宏；祖朝輔；父種〔王府紀善〕；母楊氏。嚴侍下。兄功〔百戶〕、助；弟勤、勃、勅。娶儲氏，繼娶劉氏。河南鄉試第四十二名，會試第一百十三名。

郭如川〔貫四川叙州府富順縣民籍，縣學附學生，治《詩經》，字元至，行四，年二十九，八月十八日生〕。曾祖體宗〔衛經歷，贈監察御史〕；祖瑢〔七品散官〕；父寀〔王府引禮舍人〕；前母劉氏，繼母萬氏，生母張氏。慈侍下。兄如一〔贈都察院經歷〕、如年、如堦、如登、如暄〔進士〕、如璞。娶李氏。四川鄉試第四十名，會試第一百二十七名。
translation_en:
Luo Yuren 雒于仁 [Registered as a commoner in Sanyuan County, Xi'an Prefecture, Shaanxi, originally from Jingyang County; a student of the Directorate of Education (Guozisheng), specializing in the Classic of History (Shujing). His courtesy name is Yizhong, he is the first in seniority among his brothers, and he is thirty-four years old, born on the fourth day of the fifth month]. His great-grandfather was Luo Wei [Honorary Official for Advanced Age (Shouguan)]; his grandfather was Luo Ang [repeatedly posthumously honored as Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices]; his father is Luo Zun [Minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments]; his mother was Lady Li [conferred the title of Child Nurturer (Ruren), repeatedly posthumously honored as Revered Person (Gongren)], and his stepmother is Lady Zhang [repeatedly conferred the title of Revered Person]. Both his father and stepmother are living. His younger brother is Luo Yuhan [National University Student (Jiansheng)]. He married Lady Duan. He placed 21st in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and 255th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Jia Shangzhi 賈尚志 [Registered as a commoner in Nanyang County, Nanyang Prefecture, Henan; a County Student, specializing in the Classic of History (Shujing). His courtesy name is Shishi, he is the fourth in seniority, and he is twenty-nine years old, born on the sixteenth day of the sixth month]. His great-grandfather was Jia Hong; his grandfather was Jia Lu; his father is Jia Zhen; and his mother is Lady Zhang. Both his parents are living. His younger brother is Jia Shangyou. He married Lady Pan. He placed 68th in the Henan Provincial Examination and 228th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Tian Quan 田勸 [Registered in an hereditary military officer household in the Yingchuan Guard, Henan, originally from Yingzhou, Southern Metropolitan Area (Zhili); a student of the Directorate of Education, specializing in the Classic of Poetry (Shijing). His courtesy name is Zuomin, he is the third in seniority, and he is thirty-two years old, born on the fifth day of the sixth month]. His great-grandfather was Tian Hong; his grandfather was Tian Chaofu; his father is Tian Zhong [Admonisher in a Princely Establishment (Wangfu Jishan)]; and his mother was Lady Yang. His father is living. His elder brothers are Tian Gong [Company Commander (Baihu)] and Tian Zhu; his younger brothers are Tian Qin, Tian Bo, and Tian Chi. He married Lady Chu, and remarried Lady Liu. He placed 42nd in the Henan Provincial Examination and 113th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Guo Ruchuan 郭如川 [Registered as a commoner in Fushun County, Xuzhou Prefecture, Sichuan; a Supernumerary Student of the County School, specializing in the Classic of Poetry (Shijing). His courtesy name is Yuanzhi, he is the fourth in seniority, and he is twenty-nine years old, born on the eighteenth day of the eighth month]. His great-grandfather was Guo Tizong [Guard Registrar, posthumously honored as Investigating Censor]; his grandfather was Guo Rong [Unassigned Official of the Seventh Rank]; his father was Guo Cai [Usher in a Princely Establishment (Wangfu Yinli Sheren)]; his father's first wife was Lady Liu, his stepmother was Lady Wan, and his birth mother is Lady Zhang. His mother is living. His elder brothers are Guo Ruyi [posthumously honored as Registrar of the Censorate], Guo Runian, Guo Rujie, Guo Rudeng, Guo Ruxuan [metropolitan graduate (jinshi)], and Guo Rupu. He married Lady Li. He placed 40th in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 127th in the Metropolitan Examination.

劉宇〔貫陝西漢中府金州民籍，州學生，治《春秋》，字伯大，行三，年二十八，五月初一日生〕。曾祖紳；祖萬金；父文爵〔壽官〕；母楊氏。具慶下。兄乾、坤；弟介。娶曹氏。陝西鄉試第一名，會試第二百八十三名。

translation_en:
Liu Yu 劉宇 [registered in a commoner household in Jin Department 金州, Hanzhong Prefecture 漢中府, Shaanxi; Department Student; specialized in the Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu); courtesy name Boda 伯大; third in seniority among brothers; age twenty-eight; born on the first day of the fifth month]. His great-grandfather was Liu Shen 劉紳; his grandfather was Liu Wanjin 劉萬金; his father is Liu Wenjue 劉文爵 [Longevity Official]; and his mother is Lady Yang 楊氏. Both of his parents are living. His elder brothers are Liu Qian 劉乾 and Liu Kun 劉坤; his younger brother is Liu Jie 劉介. He married Lady Cao 曹氏. He placed 1st in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and 283rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Shengshi 李盛時 [registered in a commoner household in Yi Department 易州, Baoding Prefecture 保定府, Zhili; National University Student; specialized in the Classic of Poetry (Shijing); courtesy name Bohang 伯行; first in seniority among brothers; age thirty-six; born on the eighteenth day of the tenth month]. His great-grandfather was Li Futang 李甫堂; his grandfather is Li Chong 李冲 [Longevity Official]; his father is Li Jiujing 李九經; his mother was Lady Yuan 苑氏, and his stepmothers are Lady Liu 劉氏 and Lady Lü 呂氏. Both his parents and grandparents are living. He married Lady Shi 師氏. He placed 128th in the Shuntian Prefecture 順天府 Provincial Examination and 262nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xu Yijing 許一敬 [registered in a commoner household in Haicheng County 海澄縣, Zhangzhou Prefecture 漳州府, Fujian; National University Student; specialized in the Classic of Changes (Yijing); courtesy name Sili 思禮; second in seniority among brothers; age thirty-two; born on the twelfth day of the second month]. His great-grandfather was Xu Shunde 許順德; his grandfather is Xu Bingyang 許秉陽; his father is Xu Hongding 許弘定; and his mother is Lady Chen 陳氏. Both his parents and grandparents are living. His elder brothers are Xu Wenxin 許文馨, Xu Min 許旻 [Tribute Student (gongshi)], Xu Sizheng 許思正, and Xu Sizhe 許思哲; his younger brothers are Xu Yifan 許一范, Xu Yizhu 許一洙, Xu Yiping 許一泙, Xu Yijun 許一濬, Xu Yihan 許一瀚, Xu Yican 許一澯, Xu Yidan 許一憺, Xu Yibian 許一汴, Xu Yiluo 許一洛, Xu Yijia 許一浹, Xu Yihuan 許一漶, and Xu Yiguang 許一瀇. He married Lady Zhang 張氏. He placed 17th in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 268th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Sancai 劉三才 [registered in a commoner household in Jingyang County 涇陽縣, Xi'an Prefecture 西安府, Shaanxi; National University Student; specialized in the Classic of Changes (Yijing); courtesy name Ziji 子極; fourth in seniority among brothers; age thirty-four; born on the eighth day of the eighth month]. His great-grandfather was Liu Qin 劉勤; his grandfather was Liu Tuan 劉彖 [Longevity Official]; his father is Liu Wenming 劉文明; his mother was Lady Qiang 強氏, and his stepmother was Lady Li 李氏. His father is living. His elder brothers are Liu Sanping 劉三聘 and Liu Sanwei 劉三畏; his younger brothers are Liu Sanxi 劉三錫 [Assistant Instructor], Liu Sanjie 劉三接, Liu Sanji 劉三極, Liu Sanqi 劉三奇, and Liu Sanzhang 劉三章. He married Lady Yin 殷氏. He placed 10th in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and 43rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

蔡彭〔貫福建泉州府晋江縣匠籍，國子生，治《禮記》，字敦賢，行二，年二十六，九月初二日生〕。曾祖璣；祖繼；父以德；母黃氏。永感下。兄松年；弟厯、大年、鳳年、彬年、豐年、道年、修年、彰、珍。娶黃氏。福建鄉試第八十八名，會試第二百七十五名。

translation_en:
Li Yingce 李應策 [registered in a civilian household in Pucheng County, Hua Department, Xi'an Prefecture, Shaanxi; National University Student; specialized in the Classic of Documents (Shujing); courtesy name Xianke; second in seniority among his brothers; aged twenty-seven, born on the twenty-fourth day of the eighth month]. His great-grandfather was Li Guo [Honorary Senior Citizen]; his grandfather was Li Jishi; his father is Li Tingyou [Confucian Official]; his mother is Lady Wang. Both parents are living. His elder brothers are Yingfang and Yingshu. He married Lady Lei. He placed thirty-seventh in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and three hundred and first in the Metropolitan Examination.

He Rudai 何汝岱 [registered in a military household in the Pu'an Guard, Guizhou, originally from Dangtu County, Taiping Prefecture, Southern Metropolitan Area (Zhili); Added Student of the Pu'an Department School; specialized in the Classic of Changes (Yijing); courtesy name Zongqing; fourth in seniority among his brothers; aged twenty-eight, born on the sixth day of the second month]. His great-grandfather was He Fang [Honorary Senior Citizen]; his grandfather was He Yu [posthumously honored as Gentleman for Literature and District Magistrate]; his father was He Qing [Department Magistrate]; his legal mother was Lady Wan [posthumously titled Child-Nurturess]; his birth mother is Lady Yang. His mother is living. His elder brothers are Rushang, Ruyue, and Rusong. He married Lady Hu. He placed eleventh in the Guizhou Provincial Examination and two hundred and eighty-seventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

Cai Peng 蔡彭 [registered in an artisan household in Jinjiang County, Quanzhou Prefecture, Fujian; National University Student; specialized in the Record of Rites (Liji); courtesy name Dunxian; second in seniority among his brothers; aged twenty-six, born on the second day of the ninth month]. His great-grandfather was Cai Ji; his grandfather was Cai Ji; his father was Cai Yide; his mother was Lady Huang. Both parents are deceased. His elder brother is Songnian; his younger brothers are Li, Danian, Fengnian, Binnian, Fengnian, Daonian, Xiunian, Zhang, and Zhen. He married Lady Huang. He placed eighty-eighth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and two hundred and seventy-fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Huang Tingbao 黃廷寶 [registered in a civilian household in Linchuan County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Jiangxi; National University Student; specialized in the Classic of Poetry (Shijing); courtesy name Shanqing; thirty-first in seniority in his generation; aged thirty-two, born on the twenty-third day of the second month]. His great-grandfather was Huang Yuqi; his grandfather was Huang Yao [invested as Right Assistant Minister of the Court of Judicial Review]; his father is Huang Tong; his mother was Lady Zhou; his stepmother is Lady Rao. His father and stepmother are living. His elder brothers are Tingzhen [National University Student], Tingzhu, Tingbin [National University Student], and Tingxiang; his younger brothers are Tinghe, Tingmin, Tingzan, Tingju, and Tingxuan. He married Lady Yang. He placed twenty-fourth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and one hundred and forty-eighth in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Wang Daoheng 汪道亨 (registered in an artisan household in Huaining County, An慶 Prefecture, Zhili, native of Wuyuan County, Huizhou Prefecture; a county student specializing in the Classic of Poetry (Shijing); courtesy name Ruli, fifth in his generation's birth order, aged twenty-nine, born on the sixth day of the eleventh month). His great-grandfather was Wang Min 王珉 [?]; his grandfather was Wang Zi'ang 汪子昂; his father is Wang Xi 汪析; his mother was née Pan, and his stepmother is née Shi. Both his parents are living. His elder brother is Taiheng, and his younger brothers are Cuiheng (Ceremonial Assistant in a Princely Establishment), Qianheng, and Yuheng. He married née Cheng. He placed sixty-eighth in the Yingtian Prefectural Provincial Examination and two hundred fifty-first in the Metropolitan Examination.

Lin Cai 林材 (registered in a civilian household in Min County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Fujian; a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Classic of Poetry (Shijing); courtesy name Jinren, eleventh in his generation's birth order, aged thirty-four, born on the fourth day of the third month). His great-grandfather was Lin Luo 林絡; his grandfather was Lin Sui 林燧 (Longevity Official); his father was Lin Kan 林堪 (District Magistrate); and his mother is née Chen. His mother is living. His elder brothers are Jing and Jian, and his younger brothers are Ruchong, Rulan, Rushuo, and Rukeng. He married née Chen. He placed forty-ninth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and two hundred sixty-fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Yitang 李以唐 (registered in a military household in Wu'an County, Cizhou, Zhangde Prefecture, Henan; a county student specializing in the Classic of Poetry (Shijing); courtesy name Boyao, first in his generation's birth order, aged twenty-seven, born on the ninth day of the ninth month). His great-grandfather was Li Jiang 李江; his grandfather was Li Qian 李乾; his father is Li Fan 李蕃 (Longevity Official); and his mother is née Wang. Both his parents are living. His younger brothers are Yigeng and Yikang. He married née He. He placed seventy-fourth in the Henan Provincial Examination and three hundred thirty-ninth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Bing 李炳 (registered in a civilian household in Lushi County, Henan Prefecture, Henan; a county student specializing in the Classic of History (Shujing); courtesy name Wenzhi, second in his generation's birth order, aged twenty-six, born on the fourteenth day of the fifth month). His great-grandfather was Li Que 李愨; his grandfather was Li Gui 李珪 (tribute student); his father is Li Nan 李柟; his mother was née Zheng, and his stepmother is née Zhang. Both his parents are living. His elder brother is Geng, and his younger brother is Xiu. He married née Geng. He placed thirty-sixth in the Henan Provincial Examination and two hundred first in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Huang Yingpin 黃應聘 [native of Jiangjin County, Chongqing Prefecture, Sichuan, of military registration, a supernumerary student of the county school, specializing in the Classic of Poetry (Shijing), style name Sanfu, first in generational order, aged twenty-seven, born on the third day of the tenth month]. His great-grandfather was Huang Biao; his grandfather was Huang Heling; his father is Huang Xi, and his mother is née Zeng. Both parents are living. His younger brothers are Yingyuan, Yingkui, Yingtai, Yingcong, and Yingyue. He married née Li, and subsequently married née Wang. He placed sixteenth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and two hundred ninety-first in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Yangzhi 劉養志 [native of Jiangjin County, Chongqing Prefecture, Sichuan, of civilian registration, a supernumerary student of the county school, specializing in the Classic of Documents (Shujing), style name Xiyin, first in generational order, aged twenty-seven, born on the fifth day of the twelfth month]. His great-grandfather was Liu Ao; his grandfather was Liu Zongyuan; his father is Liu Xianda, his mother was née Liu, and his stepmother is née Yu. Both father and stepmother are living. His younger brothers are Yangzhong and Yangxin. He married née Zhu. He placed thirty-third in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and two hundred ninetieth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yong Zhike 雍之可 [native of Nanchong County, Shunqing Prefecture, Sichuan, of civilian registration, a National University Student, specializing in the Classic of Changes (Yijing), style name Zijing, fourth in generational order, aged thirty-four, born on the twenty-fourth day of the second month]. His great-grandfather was Yong Benrang; his grandfather was Yong Luan [Administrative Clerk of a Guard]; his father was Yong Li [County Magistrate], his father's former wife was née Chen, and his mother was née Jiao. Both parents are deceased. His older brother is Zhixun [Annual Tribute Student], and his younger brother is Zhimin. He married née Wang. He placed fifty-first in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and two hundred ninety-ninth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chang Xin 常心 [native of Zheng Subprefecture, Kaifeng Prefecture, Henan, of civilian registration, a student of the subprefectural school, specializing in the Classic of Documents (Shujing), style name Youruo, first in generational order, aged twenty-six, born on the twenty-fourth day of the sixth month]. His great-grandfather was Chang Shen; his grandfather was Chang Jiang [Confucian Official]; his father is Chang Gui [Confucian Official], his father's former wife was née Zhang, and his mother is née Song. Both parents are living. His younger brother is Chan. He married née Wei. He placed ninth in the Henan Provincial Examination and one hundred thirty-third in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yang Yingzhong 楊應中: Registered under a military household in the Wugong Central Guard (Wugong zhongwei 武功中衞), originally from Gu'an County (Gu'an xian 固安縣), Shuntian Prefecture (Shuntian fu 順天府); a Student of the Directorate of Education (guozisheng 國子生) specializing in the Classic of Poetry (Shijing 詩經); courtesy name Zizhen 子貞, second in seniority among his brothers, aged thirty-two, born on the eighth day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather was Yang Da 達; his grandfather was Yang Duan 端; his father was Yang Zongpei 宗沛; and his mother was Lady Liu 劉氏. Both of his parents are deceased. His elder brother is Yingchen 應臣; his younger brothers are Yingkui 應奎 and Yingqi 應期. He married Lady Duan 段氏, and subsequently married Lady Duan 段氏 and Lady Han 韓氏. He placed 97th in the Shuntian Prefectural Provincial Examination and 316th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Chuchan 陳楚產: Registered under a commoner household in Macheng County (Macheng xian 麻城縣), Huangzhou Prefecture (Huangzhou fu 黃州府), Huguang 湖廣; a Student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu 春秋); courtesy name Yuedao 悅道, first in seniority among his brothers, aged thirty-two, born on the fifth day of the first month. His great-grandfather was Chen Wei 渭; his grandfather was Chen Dagui 大貴; his father is Chen Hu 瑚; and his mother was Lady Yang 楊氏. His father is living and his mother is deceased. He married Lady Mei 梅氏. He placed 70th in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 183rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Cheng Shi 程試: Registered under a commoner household in Xinhe County (Xinhe xian 新河縣), Zhending Prefecture (Zhending fu 真定府), Zhili 直隸; a County Student (xianxuesheng 縣學生) specializing in the Classic of Poetry (Shijing 詩經); courtesy name Ziyue 子躍, second in seniority among his brothers, aged thirty-one, born on the fifth day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather was Cheng Wen 文; his grandfather was Cheng Jing 敬; his father is Cheng Keqing 克清; and his mother was Lady Zhang 張氏. His father is living and his mother is deceased. His elder brother is Xing 省; his younger brothers are Ke 課, Sixun 思訓, and Sicheng 思誠. He married Lady Li 李氏. He placed 13th in the Shuntian Prefectural Provincial Examination and 185th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xing Shaomei 邢紹美: Registered under a commoner household in Luoyang County (Luoyang xian 洛陽縣), Henan Prefecture (Henan fu 河南府), Henan 河南; a Student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Classic of Changes (Yijing 易經); courtesy name Youjia 有嘉, first in seniority among his brothers, aged twenty-nine, born on the twenty-sixth day of the intercalary eleventh month. His great-grandfather was Xing Huizhi 憓之; his grandfather was Xing Si 泗 ( sacrificial attendant, shengjiguan 省祭官); his father is Xing Qili 其禮 (Confucian official, ruguan 儒官); his mother was Lady Xi 習氏; and his stepmother is Lady Duan 段氏. Both his father and stepmother are living. His younger brothers are Shao'en 紹恩, Shaoye 紹業, Shaoyou 紹祐, and Shaode 紹德. He married Lady Bu 布氏. He placed 21st in the Henan Provincial Examination and 321st in the Metropolitan Examination.

punctuated:
何偉〔貫四川重慶府涪州民籍，江西臨江府新喻縣人，州學增廣生，治《易經》，字汝器，行三，年二十八，正月初二日生〕。曾祖喻；祖本清；父和鳴；嫡母楊氏；生母黎氏。慈侍下。兄俊、傑〔省祭官〕。娶張氏。四川鄉試第十二名，會試第二百二十九名。

文運熙〔貫陝西西安府邠州三水縣軍籍，國子生，治《詩經》，字時雍，行四，年三十九，九月初二日生〕。曾祖錦〔壽官〕；祖守經；父官〔歲貢生〕；母張氏。永感下。兄運開〔學正，封禮部主事〕、運盛〔歲貢生〕、運際。娶馬氏。陝西鄉試第十二名，會試第三百七名。

屠如虹〔貫萬全靖所籍，浙江杭州府仁和縣人，順天府學生，治《易經》，字見辰，行四，年三十二，正月初五日生〕。曾祖祥〔壽官〕；祖琳；父子臣；母俞氏。具慶下。兄洲〔州吏目〕、臯、經鶴；弟文虹、晴虹、雲虹、有益、錫光。娶沈氏。順天府鄉試第一百十四名，會試第三百九名。

徐準〔貫山東濟南府新城縣匠籍，國子生，治《詩經》，字子式，行一，年三十二，八月初十日生〕。曾祖表；祖雄；父朋；母羅氏。慈侍下。弟化行〔貢士〕。娶蔡氏，繼娶賈氏。山東鄉試第四十二名，會試第二百十七名。
translation_en:
He Wei 何偉 (registered under a commoner household in Fuzhou, Chongqing Prefecture, Sichuan, originally from Xinyu County, Linjiang Prefecture, Jiangxi; an added student of the Subprefectural School specializing in the Classic of Changes [Yijing]; courtesy name Ruqi, third in seniority among his brothers, aged twenty-eight, born on the second day of the first month). His great-grandfather was He Yu; his grandfather was He Benqing; his father was He Heming; his legal mother was Lady Yang; his birth mother is Lady Li. His mother is alive while his father is deceased. His elder brothers are He Jun and He Jie (Sacrificial Attendant). He married Lady Zhang. He placed 12th in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 229th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wen Yunxi 文運熙 (registered under a military household in Sanshui County, Binzhou, Xi'an Prefecture, Shaanxi; a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Classic of Poetry [Shijing]; courtesy name Shiyong, fourth in seniority among his brothers, aged thirty-nine, born on the second day of the ninth month). His great-grandfather was Wen Jin (Honorary Official for Longevity); his grandfather was Wen Shoujing; his father was Wen Guan (Annual Tribute Student); his mother was Lady Zhang. Both of his parents are deceased. His elder brothers are Wen Yunkai (Subprefectural Director of Studies, granted the title of Secretary in the Ministry of Rites), Wen Yunsheng (Annual Tribute Student), and Wen Yunji. He married Lady Ma. He placed 12th in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and 307th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Tu Ruhong 屠如虹 (registered under the Wanquan Huai'an Guard / Jing Battalion [?] household, originally from Renhe County, Hangzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang; a student of the Shuntian Prefectural School specializing in the Classic of Changes [Yijing]; courtesy name Jianchen, fourth in seniority among his brothers, aged thirty-two, born on the fifth day of the first month). His great-grandfather was Tu Xiang (Honorary Official for Longevity); his grandfather was Tu Lin; his father is Tu Zichen; his mother is Lady Yu. Both of his parents are alive. His elder brothers are Tu Zhou (Subprefectural Chief of Police), Tu Gao, and Tu Jinghe; his younger brothers are Tu Wenhong, Tu Qinghong, Tu Yunhong, Tu Youyi, and Tu Xiguang. He married Lady Shen. He placed 114th in the Shuntian Provincial Examination and 309th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xu Zhun 徐準 (registered under an artisan household in Xincheng County, Jinan Prefecture, Shandong; a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Classic of Poetry [Shijing]; courtesy name Zishi, first in seniority among his brothers, aged thirty-two, born on the tenth day of the eighth month). His great-grandfather was Xu Biao; his grandfather was Xu Xiong; his father was Xu Peng; his mother is Lady Luo. His mother is alive while his father is deceased. His younger brother is Xu Huaxing (Tribute Scholar). He married Lady Cai, and took Lady Jia as his second wife. He placed 42nd in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 217th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Huang E 黃萼 [registered in a commoner household in Longxi County, Zhangzhou Prefecture, Fujian; Student of the Directorate of Imperial Academy (guozisheng); specialized in the Book of Changes (Yijing); courtesy name Guoying; third in his generation; age thirty-two, born on the twenty-fifth day of the ninth month]. His great-grandfather was Rongqing; his grandfather was Chunjie; his father was Zuo, and his mother was née Xu. His mother is living. His elder brothers are Fen and Mao, and his younger brothers are Cui and Bao. He married née Zhang. He placed fifteenth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and one hundred fifteenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Jie 王堦 [registered in a military household in Jingshan County, Chengtian Prefecture, Huguang; Student of the Directorate of Imperial Academy; specialized in the Book of Odes (Shijing); courtesy name Zhenji; first in his generation; age twenty-eight, born on the sixteenth day of the first month]. His great-grandfather was Dashou; his grandfather was Cai; his father is Zongjing [granted cap and belt by special grace], his mother was née Xu, and his stepmother is née Shu. His father and stepmother are both living. His younger brothers are Du, Jiong, and Kan. He married née Xia. He placed sixteenth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and two hundred fifty-seventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Siyu 劉思瑜 [registered in a commoner household in Anfu County, Ji'an Prefecture, Jiangxi; Instructor (jiaoyu) of the Confucian School of Yongding County, Tingzhou Prefecture; specialized in the Book of Documents (Shujing); courtesy name Bomei; first in his generation; age thirty-one, born on the thirteenth day of the first month]. His great-grandfather was Shengguang; his grandfather was Jizhan; his father is Quan, and his mother is née Zhu. Both parents are living. His younger brothers are Siqiu, Sigui, Siyuan, and Siyao. He married née Zhu. He placed eighty-third in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and two hundred thirty-third in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zheng Guojun 鄭國俊 [registered in a commoner household in Xiezhou, Pingyang Prefecture, Shanxi; Subprefectural Confucian Student (zhouxuesheng); specialized in the Book of Documents (Shujing); courtesy name Junyu; first in his generation; age twenty-six, born on the seventh day of the ninth month]. His great-grandfather was Zan; his grandfather was Ji; his father is Mao [Subprefectural Instructor (xuezheng)], his father's former wives were née Pu and née Wei, and his mother is née Hou. Both parents are living. His younger brother is Guoyan. He married née Guo. He placed fifty-second in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and three hundred forty-sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

蔣薦 貫江西吉安守禦千戶所官籍廬陵縣人 國子生
治易經字君受行三年二十八七月初九日生
曾祖持 祖鑾 父源 母胡氏 繼母嚴氏
永感下 兄蘭〔指揮 僉事〕 弟萃 莊 娶王氏
江西鄉試第十一名 會試第十四名
梁雲龍 貫廣東瓊州府瓊山縣民籍 府學生
治易經字會可行二年三十六四月二十日生
曾祖琛 祖崑 父文懷 母馮氏
永感下 兄雲鵬 必大 弟必強〔知縣〕 雲鴻 娶王氏
廣東鄉試第三十三名 會試第一百八十一名
punctuated:
李爲芝〔貫陝西西安府華州匠籍，州學生，治《易經》，字明瑞，行一，年二十八，二月初三日生〕。曾祖威，祖清〔壽官〕，父岳，母王氏。永感下。弟爲桂〔義官〕、爲楠、爲桐。娶薛氏。陝西鄉試第十名，會試第二百十六名。
岳萬階〔貫山東東昌府濮州朝城縣民籍，縣學生，治《春秋》，字允升，行二，年二十八，十月初一日生〕。曾祖位，祖事堯〔壽官〕，父電，母李氏，繼母周氏。重慶下。兄萬仞，弟萬陛、萬年、萬鍾、萬選。娶李氏。山東鄉試第二十二名，會試第二百三十九名。
蔣薦〔貫江西吉安守禦千戶所官籍，廬陵縣人，國子生，治《易經》，字君受，行三，年二十八，七月初九日生〕。曾祖持，祖盤，父源，母胡氏，繼母嚴氏。永感下。兄蘭〔指揮僉事〕，弟萃、莊。娶王氏。江西鄉試第十一名，會試第十四名。
梁雲龍〔貫廣東瓊州府瓊山縣民籍，府學生，治《易經》，字會可，行二，年三十六，四月二十日生〕。曾祖琛，祖崑，父文懷，母馮氏。永感下。兄雲鵬、必大，弟必強〔知縣〕、雲鴻。娶王氏。廣東鄉試第三十三名，會試第一百八十一名。
translation_en:
Li Weizhi 李爲芝 (registered in an artisan household in Huazhou, Xi'an Prefecture, Shaanxi; a Subprefectural Student specializing in the Classic of Changes (Yijing); courtesy name Mingrui, first in seniority; aged twenty-eight, born on the third day of the second month). His great-grandfather was Li Wei; his grandfather was Li Qing (Honorary Official for Longevity); his father was Li Yue; and his mother was Lady Wang. Both of his parents are deceased. His younger brothers are Li Weigui (Righteous Official), Li Weinan, and Li Weitong. He married Lady Xue. He placed tenth in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and two hundred and sixteenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yue Wanjie 岳萬階 (registered in a civilian household in Chaocheng County, Puzhou, Dongchang Prefecture, Shandong; a County Student specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu); courtesy name Yunsheng, second in seniority; aged twenty-eight, born on the first day of the tenth month). His great-grandfather was Yue Wei; his grandfather was Yue Shiyao (Honorary Official for Longevity); his father is Yue Dian; his mother was Lady Li; and his stepmother is Lady Zhou. His grandparents and parents are living. His elder brother is Yue Wanren, and his younger brothers are Yue Wanbi, Yue Wannian, Yue Wanzhong, and Yue Wanxuan. He married Lady Li. He placed twenty-second in the Shandong Provincial Examination and two hundred and thirty-ninth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Jiang Jian 蔣薦 (registered in a military officer's household in the Ji'an Independent Battalion, a native of Luling County, Jiangxi; a Directorate Student specializing in the Classic of Changes (Yijing); courtesy name Junshou, third in seniority; aged twenty-eight, born on the ninth day of the seventh month). His great-grandfather was Jiang Chi; his grandfather was Jiang Pan; his father was Jiang Yuan; his mother was Lady Hu; and his stepmother was Lady Yan. Both of his parents are deceased. His elder brother is Jiang Lan (Assistant Guard Commander), and his younger brothers are Jiang Cui and Jiang Zhuang. He married Lady Wang. He placed eleventh in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and fourteenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liang Yunlong 梁雲龍 (registered in a civilian household in Qiongshan County, Qiongzhou Prefecture, Guangdong; a Prefectural Student specializing in the Classic of Changes (Yijing); courtesy name Huike, second in seniority; aged thirty-six, born on the twentieth day of the fourth month). His great-grandfather was Liang Chen; his grandfather was Liang Kun; his father was Liang Wenhuai; and his mother was Lady Feng. Both of his parents are deceased. His elder brothers are Liang Yunpeng and Liang Bida, and his younger brothers are Liang Biqiang (District Magistrate) and Liang Yunhong. He married Lady Wang. He placed thirty-third in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and one hundred and eighty-first in the Metropolitan Examination.

title: 萬曆十一年進士登科錄
text:
皇帝制曰朕聞治本
於道道本於德古
今論治者必折衷
於孔子孔子告魯
君為政在九經而
===
歸本於三達德至
宋臣司馬光言人
君大德有三曰仁
曰明曰武果與孔
子合歟光歷事三
alt_text:
皇帝制曰朕聞治本
於道道本於德古
今論治者必折衷
於孔子孔子告魯

===

曰明曰武果與孔
子合歟光歷事三
punctuated: 皇帝制曰：「朕聞治本於道，道本於德。古今論治者，必折衷於孔子。孔子告魯君為政在九經，而歸本於三達德。至宋臣司馬光，言人君大德有三，曰仁、曰明、曰武，果與孔子合歟？光歷事三
translation_en: The Emperor's decree reads: "We have heard that good governance is rooted in the Way, and the Way is rooted in virtue. Those of ancient and modern times who discuss governance must take Confucius as their standard of judgment. Confucius told the ruler of Lu that conducting government lies in the nine standard rules, and traced their root back to the three universal virtues. Coming down to the Song-dynasty minister Sima Guang 司馬光, he stated that the great virtues of a ruler are three: namely benevolence, discernment, and martial vigor. Does this truly accord with Confucius? Guang successively served three…

title: 萬曆十一年進士登科錄
text:
朝三以其言獻自
謂至精至要矣然
朕觀古記可異焉
曰其仁如天其智
如神曰明物察倫
===
由仁義行曰其仁
可親其言可信皆
未及武也獨自商
以下有天錫勇智
執競維烈之稱豈

punctuated: 朝，三以其言獻，自謂至精至要矣。然朕觀古記，可異焉：曰「其仁如天，其智如神」；曰「明物察倫，由仁義行」；曰「其仁可親，其言可信」，皆未及武也。獨自商以下，有「天錫勇智」、「執競維烈」之稱，豈
translation_en: …three reigns, three times presented these words of his, deeming them the most refined and essential principles. Yet when We examine the ancient records, there is reason to find this strange: where it is said, "His benevolence was like Heaven, his wisdom like the spirits"; where it is said, "He clearly understood all things and discerned human relationships, acting out of benevolence and righteousness"; and where it is said, "His benevolence could be cherished, his words could be trusted"—none of these make mention of martial vigor. Only from the Shang dynasty onward do there appear such praises as "Heaven endowed him with valor and wisdom" and "Holding fast to strength, how glorious was his achievement!" Could it be that…

title: 萬曆十一年進士登科錄
text:
至後王始尚武歟
近世偉畧隆基之
主或寬仁愛人知
人善任或明明廟
謨赳赳雄斷或迹
===
比湯武治幾成康
或仁孝友愛聰明
豁達則洵美矣而
三德未純然亦足
以肇造洪緒何也
alt_text:
至後王始尚武歟
近世偉畧隆基之
主或寬仁愛人知
人善任或明明廟
謨赳赳雄斷或迹
===
比湯武治幾成康
或仁孝友愛聰明
睿達則洵美矣而
三德未純然亦足
以肇造洪緒何也
punctuated: 至後王始尚武歟？近世偉畧隆基之主，或寬仁愛人、知人善任，或明明廟謨、赳赳雄斷，或迹比湯、武，治幾成、康，或仁孝友愛、聰明豁達，則洵美矣；而三德未純，然亦足以肇造洪緒，何也？
translation_en: … only with the later kings that martial valor first came to be esteemed? Among the sovereigns of later ages who possessed grand strategies and established flourishing foundations: some were寬 (tolerant) and benevolent, loving the people, and perceptive in recognizing talent and employing it well; some were brilliant in their court counsels and valiant in their heroic decisiveness; some matched Tang [of Shang] and Wu [of Zhou] in their deeds, with governance nearly equal to that of Cheng and Kang [of Zhou]; and some were benevolent, filial, and fraternal, as well as intelligent, perceptive, and magnanimous. These qualities were truly admirable; yet even though they did not possess the three virtues in complete purity, they were still able to found great dynastic enterprises. Why is this?

title: 萬曆十一年進士登科錄
text:
其守成纘業者似
又弗如或以仁稱
如漢文帝宋仁宗
以明稱如漢明帝
唐明皇以武稱如
===
漢武帝唐武宗獨
具一德而亦增光
宗祊何也彼所謂
兼三者則治闕一
則衰二則危毋亦
alt_text:
其守成繼業者似
又弗如或以仁稱
如漢文帝宋仁宗
以明稱如漢明帝
唐明皇以武稱如
===
漢武帝唐武宗獨
具一德而亦增光
宗祏何也彼所謂
兼三者則治闕一
則衰二則危毋亦
punctuated: 其守成纘業者，似又弗如。或以仁稱，如漢文帝、宋仁宗；以明稱，如漢明帝、唐明皇；以武稱，如漢武帝、唐武宗。獨具一德，而亦增光宗祊，何也？彼所謂兼三者則治，闕一則衰，二則危，毋亦
translation_en: As for those who preserved the accomplishments of their predecessors and continued the dynastic enterprise, they seem to have been even less able to match them. Some were renowned for their benevolence, such as Emperor Wen of Han (漢文帝) and Emperor Renzong of Song (宋仁宗); some were renowned for their perspicacity, such as Emperor Ming of Han (漢明帝) and Emperor Minghuang of Tang (唐明皇); and some were renowned for their martial vigor, such as Emperor Wu of Han (漢武帝) and Emperor Wuzong of Tang (唐武宗). Each possessed only one of these virtues, yet they too brought added glory to their ancestral temples—why is this? That saying that combining all three leads to order, lacking one leads to decline, and lacking two leads to peril—is it not…

title: 萬曆十一年進士登科錄
text:
責人太備歟又有
疏六戒者曰戒太
察戒無斷陳九弊
者曰眩聰明勵威
强上六事者曰不
===
喜兵刑不用智數
其於三德果有當
否歟朕乘乾御極
十有一年於兹夕
惕晨興永懷至理
alt_text:
責人太備歟又有
踈六戒者曰戒太
察戒無斷陳九弊
者曰聰明勵威
強上六事者曰不
===
喜兵刑不用智數
其於三德果有當
否歟朕秉乾御極
十有一年於茲夕
惕晨興永懷至理
punctuated: 責人太備歟？又有疏六戒者曰：「戒太察、戒無斷。」陳九弊者曰：「眩聰明、勵威强。」上六事者曰：「不喜兵刑、不用智數。」其於三德果有當否歟？朕乘乾御極，十有一年於兹。夕惕晨興，永懷至理。
translation_en:
…demanding too much perfection of a person? Furthermore, there was one who submitted a memorial on the "Six Admonitions," saying: "Guard against excessive scrutiny; guard against indecisiveness." Another set forth the "Nine Malpractices," saying: "Making a show of intelligence and acuity; straining after awesome might." And another presented the "Six Matters," saying: "Do not delight in military force and punishments; do not employ shrewdness and artifice." How well do these remarks actually accord with the Three Virtues?

We have occupied the imperial throne and ruled the realm for eleven years now. Vigilant by night and rising at dawn, We constantly set Our heart on supreme governance. …

title: 萬曆十一年進士登科錄
text:
然紀綱飭而吏滋
玩田野墾而民滋
困學校肅而士滋
偷邉鄙寧而兵滋
譁督捕嚴而盜滋
===
起厥咎安在豈朕
仁未溥歟明或蔽
歟當機而少斷歟
夫一切繩天下以
三尺則害仁然專
alt_text:
然紀綱飭而吏滋
玩田野墾而民滋
困學校肅而士滋
偷邉鄙寧而兵滋
譁督捕嚴而盗滋
===
起厥咎安在豈朕
仁未溥歟明或蔽
歟當機而少斷歟
夫一切繩天下以
三尺則害仁然專
punctuated: 然紀綱飭而吏滋玩，田野墾而民滋困，學校肅而士滋偷，邉鄙寧而兵滋譁，督捕嚴而盜滋起，厥咎安在？豈朕仁未溥歟？明或蔽歟？當機而少斷歟？夫一切繩天下以三尺則害仁，然專
translation_en: Yet though discipline and institutions are rectified, officials grow increasingly negligent; though farmlands are opened up, the people grow increasingly distressed; though schools are regulated with solemnity, scholars grow increasingly lax; though the frontiers are tranquil, soldiers grow increasingly mutinous; and though the supervision of arrests is strict, bandits arise in increasing numbers. Wherein lies the fault for this? Is it that Our benevolence has not yet been universally extended? That Our discernment is perhaps obscured? Or that at critical moments We lack decisiveness? Now, if in all matters one binds the realm with the three-foot statutory code, it harms benevolence; yet if one exclusively…

title: 萬曆十一年進士登科錄
text:
務尚德緩刑恐非
仁而流於姑息一
切納污藏疾則害
明然專務發奸擿
伏恐非明而傷於
===
===
煩苛一切寬柔因
任則害武然專務
用威克愛恐非武
而病於亢暴是用
詔所司進多士詳
alt_text:

仁而流於姑息一
切納汚藏疾則害
明然專務發奸擿
伏恐非明而傷於
===
煩苛一切寬柔因
任則害武然專務
用威克愛恐非武
而病於亢暴是用
詔所司進多士詳
punctuated: 務尚德緩刑，恐非仁而流於姑息；一切納污藏疾，則害明，然專務發奸擿伏，恐非明而傷於煩苛；一切寬柔因任，則害武，然專務用威克愛，恐非武而病於亢暴。是用詔所司進多士，詳
translation_en: …devote oneself to prizing virtue and relaxing punishments, I fear this is not benevolence, and slips into laxity. If one tolerates all filth and harbors all flaws without exception, it harms perspicacity; yet if one exclusively devotes oneself to exposing treachery and uncovering hidden offenses, I fear this is not perspicacity, and suffers from vexatious harshness. If one relies on leniency, complaisance, and passive acquiescence without exception, it harms martial vigor; yet if one exclusively devotes oneself to letting severity overcome affection, I fear this is not martial vigor, and suffers from overbearing tyranny. Therefore, I have decreed that the authorities present the many scholars, carefully…

title: 萬曆十一年進士登科錄
text:
延於廷諏以此道
諸士得不勉思而
茂明之其為朕闡
典謨之㫖推帝王
之憲稽當世之務
===
悉陳勿諱朕眷兹
洽聞將裁覽而采
行焉
alt_text:
延於廷諏以此道
諸士得不勉思而
茂明之其爲朕闡
典謨之旨推帝王
之憲稽當世之務
悉陳勿諱朕眷兹
洽聞將裁覽而采
行焉
punctuated: 延於廷，諏以此道。諸士得不勉思而茂明之？其為朕闡典謨之㫖，推帝王之憲，稽當世之務，悉陳勿諱。朕眷兹洽聞，將裁覽而采行焉。
translation_en: …receive you in the palace courtyard to consult with you on this Way. How could you scholars not strive to ponder this and abundantly clarify it? Expound for Us the purport of the canons and counsels, deduce the institutions of the emperors and kings, and examine the affairs of the present age—set forth everything in full and hold nothing back. We hold in high regard such broad learning, and shall personally review your responses and select from them to put into practice.

title: 萬曆十一年進士登科錄
text:
臣朱國祚
臣對臣聞帝王之繼天以凝命也必全君德
以端天下之大本而後可以弘經遠之猷必
酌時宜以操天下之大機而後可以致綦隆
之治何謂大本斂之淵微之內而達諸應感
之交慈祥愷悌盎然而可親精明瑩徹炯然
而無蔽剛毅果斷確然而不移凝神於端莊
靜一之中而渾融無間者是已何謂大機審
諸時勢之宜而推諸運量之際兼容併包不
流於姑息先見玄覽不失於苛察總攬獨斷
===
不嫌於刻覈觀變於動靜陰陽之妙而化裁
無迹者是已全德以為之主則酬酢萬幾錯
綜萬變一精神性術之流動而不患於出治
之無本隨時以制其宜則上協天道下合人
情乃轉移化導之微權而不患於致治之無
機治古帝王所以不下階序而化行若神躋
一世於泰山之安而九圍式命鞏國祚於苞
桑之固而萬國傾心用此道耳藉令為治而
不本之以德則雖有所設施厝注亦將墮於
私智小術而推行無準何以端天下之治本

臣對：臣聞帝王之繼天以凝命也，必全君德以端天下之大本，而後可以弘經遠之猷；必酌時宜以操天下之大機，而後可以致綦隆之治。何謂大本？斂之淵微之內，而達諸應感之交；慈祥愷悌，盎然而可親；精明瑩徹，炯然而無蔽；剛毅果斷，確然而不移；凝神於端莊靜一之中，而渾融無間者是已。何謂大機？審諸時勢之宜，而推諸運量之際；兼容併包，不流於姑息；先見玄覽，不失於苛察；總攬獨斷，不嫌於刻覈；觀變於動靜陰陽之妙，而化裁無迹者是已。全德以為之主，則酬酢萬幾、錯綜萬變，一精神性術之流動，而不患於出治之無本；隨時以制其宜，則上協天道、下合人情，乃轉移化導之微權，而不患於致治之無機。治古帝王所以不下階序，而化行若神，躋一世於泰山之安，而九圍式命；鞏國祚於苞桑之固，而萬國傾心，用此道耳。藉令為治而不本之以德，則雖有所設施厝注，亦將墮於私智小術，而推行無準，何以端天下之治本，
translation_en:
Your servant Zhu Guozuo 朱國祚.

Your servant replies: Your servant has heard that when emperors and kings succeed to Heaven in consolidating the Mandate, they must perfect the sovereign's virtue to rectify the great foundation of the realm, and only then can they broaden their far-reaching plans of governance; they must weigh what is appropriate to the times to grasp the great pivot of the realm, and only then can they bring about an era of supreme prosperity. What is meant by the "great foundation"? It is that which is gathered within the profound and subtle interior and extended to the juncture of stimulus and response: benevolent, kind, and genial, overflowing with approachability; clear-sighted and luminous, shining without obscuration; resolute and decisive, steadfast and unswerving—concentrating one's spirit in dignified gravity and tranquil unity, blended into a seamless whole. What is meant by the "great pivot"? It is that which is examined in light of what suits the trends of the times and applied in the course of deliberation and management: all-embracing and inclusive without lapsing into lax indulgence; far-sighted and profoundly perceptive without erring into petty scrutiny; exercising comprehensive control and sole decision-making without incurring the suspicion of harsh exactitude—observing transformations in the subtle interplay of movement and stillness, yin and yang, while tailoring and shaping without leaving a trace. When perfected virtue serves as the master, then in responding to ten thousand affairs and weaving together ten thousand changes, all is the seamless flow of one's spirit, nature, and inner art, and there is no worry that governance lacks a foundation. When one institutes what is fitting in accordance with the times, then above it harmonizes with the Way of Heaven and below it accords with human sentiment; this is the subtle authority of transforming and guiding, and there is no worry that the attainment of order lacks a pivot. The reason the emperors and kings of well-governed antiquity did not descend the steps of their halls, yet their transformative influence operated like a spirit—raising a whole generation to the security of Mount Tai so that the nine regions took their commands as a model, and consolidating the dynastic fortune to the firmness of clustered mulberry roots so that the myriad states inclined their hearts toward them—was simply that they employed this Way. Suppose one were to pursue governance without rooting it in virtue: then even if there were measures enacted and arrangements put in place, they would sink into private cleverness and petty techniques, lacking any standard in their implementation; how then could one rectify the foundation of governance for the realm…

title: 萬曆十一年進士登科錄
text:
而躋一世於雍熙修德而不運之以機則雖
有所謀謨智慮亦將流於偏見寡識而泛應
無權何以弘天下之遠猷而登斯世於上理
此晚近世之陋規非上聖之宏圖而極治之
要道也欽惟
皇帝陛下
稟剛健中正之資
備文武聖神之德
孜孜問學寒暑不替而維皇之極已端
事事講求鉅細不遺而望道之心甚切

廓嚴肅之威與風霆而並迅固已四三王六五

欽惟皇帝陛下：稟剛健中正之資，備文武聖神之德；孜孜問學，寒暑不替，而維皇之極已端；事事講求，鉅細不遺，而望道之心甚切；溥弘敷之澤，與河海而同深；廓嚴肅之威，與風霆而並迅。固已四三王、六五帝，而超出於尋常萬萬矣！乃猶不自滿假，進臣等於廷，俯賜清問：上嘉虞、周之盛王，下逮漢、唐之令主；始之以孔子九經之言，而繼之以司馬光三劄之語，而於治道之所尚特惓惓焉。臣有以仰窺陛下之心，即虞帝疇咨之心，即周王訪道之心，而
translation_en:
…and elevate the entire generation to harmonious prosperity? Conversely, if one cultivates virtue without setting it in motion through the pivotal mechanisms of action, then even if there are counsels, plans, and wise deliberations, they too will degenerate into partial views and narrow understanding, lacking the flexibility to respond broadly to circumstances; how then could one expand far-reaching plans for the realm and raise this world to supreme order? Such are the vulgar conventions of recent ages, not the grand design of a supreme sage or the essential Way of ultimate governance.

Reverently I reflect that Your Imperial Majesty is endowed with a nature of firm strength and central rectitude, and possesses the virtues of civil and martial accomplishment, sageliness, and spiritual splendour. Tirelessly You pursue learning and inquiry without lapse through winter cold and summer heat, so that the Sovereign's standard of perfection is already upright; in every affair You investigate thoroughly, overlooking neither great nor small, so that Your heart's longing for the Way is most earnest. You spread broadly diffused beneficence as deep as the rivers and seas, and extend stern and solemn majesty as swift as the wind and thunder. Truly You have already become a fourth to the Three Kings and a sixth to the Five Emperors, surpassing the ordinary ten thousand times over! Yet still You do not rest in self-satisfaction, advancing Your servants and others into the Court and graciously bestowing Your clear inquiry: looking upward, You praise the flourishing kings of Yu [Shun] and Zhou, and reaching downward, You touch upon the fine rulers of Han and Tang; You begin with Confucius's words on the Nine Standards and continue with Sima Guang's remarks in his three memorials, showing especial earnestness regarding what ought to be prized in the Way of governance. Your servant is thus able to look up and discern that Your Majesty's mind is none other than the mind of the Sovereign of Yu inquiring of his ministers, and none other than the mind of the King of Zhou seeking the Way, whereas…

title: 萬曆十一年進士登科錄
text:
漢唐宋諸君無足數矣臣也竊伏蓬藿志切
輸忠凡吏治之汚隆人心之淳漓與夫養士
興賢之法足兵弭盜之方其究於心久矣卽
不問願有所陳說況
聖問彰彰如是臣敢不披瀝以對臣聞古之聖王
之御世也未嘗以無本之治治之故紀綱法
度禮樂刑政要皆一本於心未嘗以執一之
治治之故剛柔互用仁義竝行要皆可適於
治此智仁勇相濟以有成仁明武相須以竝
濟宣聖所以上接堯舜之統而司馬光所以
===
仰承洙泗之傳者率是道也是故唐虞之世
天下號極治矣當其時黎民於變萬邦咸寧
和氣盈於域中文命敷於四海又安用夫武
哉顧無武之名而有神武之運精明果斷之
意常寓於湛恩濊澤之中其仁如天其智如
神堯之所以蕩蕩難名也而若時之命不以
畀於啓明之胤子又何嚴乎明物察倫由仁
義行舜之所以巍巍莫與也而四凶之罪不
少假於象刑之惟明又何毅乎其仁可親其
言可信禹之所以祗台德先也而防風之誅

punctuated:
漢、唐、宋諸君無足數矣！臣也竊伏蓬藿，志切輸忠，凡吏治之汚隆、人心之淳漓，與夫養士興賢之法、足兵弭盜之方，其究於心久矣。卽不問，願有所陳說；況聖問彰彰如是，臣敢不披瀝以對？
臣聞古之聖王之御世也，未嘗以無本之治治之，故紀綱、法度、禮樂、刑政，要皆一本於心；未嘗以執一之治治之，故剛柔互用、仁義竝行，要皆可適於治。此智、仁、勇相濟以有成，仁、明、武相須以竝濟，宣聖所以上接堯、舜之統，而司馬光所以仰承洙、泗之傳者，率是道也。
是故唐、虞之世，天下號極治矣。當其時，黎民於變，萬邦咸寧，和氣盈於域中，文命敷於四海，又安用夫武哉？顧無武之名，而有神武之運，精明果斷之意，常寓於湛恩濊澤之中。其仁如天，其智如神，堯之所以蕩蕩難名也；而若時之命，不以畀於啓明之胤子，又何嚴乎！明物察倫，由仁義行，舜之所以巍巍莫與也；而四凶之罪，不少假於象刑之惟明，又何毅乎！其仁可親，其言可信，禹之所以祗台德先也；而防風之誅，
translation_en:
… the monarchs of the Han, Tang, and Song are not worth counting! While your servant lived hidden away in humble obscurity, my ambition was earnestly set on offering loyalty. Everything concerning the corruption or flourishing of official administration, the purity or degeneracy of popular morale, as well as the methods for nurturing scholars and promoting the worthy, and the strategies for maintaining sufficient troops and quelling bandits—I have investigated these in my mind for a long time. Even if not asked, I would have wished to set forth my views; how much more so when Your Sacred Majesty's inquiry is as brilliantly manifest as this—how could your servant dare not lay bare my heart in reply?
Your servant has heard that when the sage kings of antiquity governed the world, they never governed it with a governance lacking a fundamental root; therefore, regulatory principles, laws and institutions, rites and music, punishments and administration in essence were all rooted in the mind. Nor did they ever govern it with a governance that clung to a single method; therefore, firmness and gentleness were used alternately, and benevolence and righteousness were practiced side by side, so that in essence all could be adapted to good governance. Thus wisdom, benevolence, and courage complemented one another to achieve success, and benevolence, discernment, and martial vigor depended on one another to advance together. That whereby the Exalted Sage [Confucius] carried on the succession of Yao and Shun above, and that whereby Sima Guang reverently received the transmission of the Zhu and Si rivers [i.e., the Confucian school]—all followed this Way.
Therefore, in the era of Tang and Yu [Yao and Shun], the realm was acclaimed as being in a state of utmost governance. At that time, the black-haired people were transformed, the myriad states were all at peace, harmonious vital energy filled the realm, and civilizing mandates were spread throughout the Four Seas—what need was there to employ martial force? Yet while lacking the name of martial force, they possessed the operation of divine martial vigor, and a spirit of keen discernment and decisive resolution constantly resided within their profound grace and overflowing beneficence. "His benevolence was like Heaven, his wisdom like a spirit"—this was why Yao was vast and beyond naming; yet the mandate to accord with the times he did not bestow upon his enlightened heir Apparent [Dan Zhu]—how stern was that! "Clearly understanding things and investigating human relationships, acting out of benevolence and righteousness"—this was why Shun was lofty and beyond compare; yet the crimes of the Four Fiends were not in the least pardoned under the clear manifestation of his statutory punishments—how resolute was that! "His benevolence was approachable, his words trustworthy"—this was why Yu reverently took virtue as his priority; yet in the execution of Fangfeng, …

title: 萬曆十一年進士登科錄
text:
不少貸於會稽之後至又何肅乎是堯舜禹
非不用武也乃所以善用其武也商周之世
天下稱至治矣當是時天下大定邦家輯寧
陳師於南巢觀兵於牧野豈非用武哉顧有
武之迹而無尚武之心寬厚博大之規常寓
於肅清戡定之內天錫勇智湯之所以奉若
天命也而克寬克仁彰信兆民則仲虺稱之
矣執競維烈武之所以永清四海也而不泄
於邇無忘於遠則孟軻贊之矣是湯武非用
武也乃所以善成其仁智也裔是而降創業
===
之主肇造洪緒以開一代之治者雖其德未
底於純全之域而亦足以致治故漢高帝寬
仁愛人知人善任則五年而成帝業光武明
明廟謨赳赳雄斷則數載而克中興迹比湯
武治幾成康者唐太宗也而貞觀之治卒開
唐氏之業仁孝友愛聰明豁達者宋太祖也
而仁厚之澤卒貽數葉之安之數君者或以
嚴明造大業或以忠厚垂鴻休彼三德之用
夫固各有攸當也守成之主嗣守先業以繼
一代之統者雖其德未造於純粹之歸而亦

punctuated:
不少貸於會稽之後至，又何肅乎！是堯、舜、禹非不用武也，乃所以善用其武也。商、周之世，天下稱至治矣。當是時，天下大定，邦家輯寧，陳師於南巢，觀兵於牧野，豈非用武哉？顧有武之迹而無尚武之心，寬厚博大之規，常寓於肅清戡定之內。天錫勇智，湯之所以奉若天命也；而克寬克仁，彰信兆民，則仲虺稱之矣。執競維烈，武之所以永清四海也；而不泄於邇，無忘於遠，則孟軻贊之矣。是湯、武非用武也，乃所以善成其仁智也。

裔是而降，創業之主，肇造洪緒以開一代之治者，雖其德未底於純全之域，而亦足以致治。故漢高帝寬仁愛人，知人善任，則五年而成帝業；光武明明廟謨，赳赳雄斷，則數載而克中興。迹比湯、武，治幾成、康者，唐太宗也，而貞觀之治卒開唐氏之業；仁孝友愛，聰明豁達者，宋太祖也，而仁厚之澤卒貽數葉之安。之數君者，或以嚴明造大業，或以忠厚垂鴻休，彼三德之用，夫固各有攸當也。守成之主，嗣守先業以繼一代之統者，雖其德未造於純粹之歸，而亦
translation_en:
…was not in the slightest pardoned for arriving late at Guiji—how solemn that was! Thus, Yao, Shun, and Yu did not refrain from using martial force; rather, this was how they excelled in using their martial force. In the eras of the Shang and Zhou dynasties, the realm was acclaimed as having reached supreme governance. At that time, the realm was greatly settled and the state was harmonious and tranquil. Yet arraying troops at Nanchao and displaying arms at Muye—was this not the use of martial force? However, they bore the traces of martial force without a heart that exalted martiality, and grand plans of generosity and breadth of mind constantly resided within their sweeping pacification and suppression of disorder. "Heaven endowed him with valor and wisdom"—this was how Tang the Successful reverently followed the Mandate of Heaven; yet that he was able to be generous and benevolent, manifesting trustworthiness to the myriad people, was praised by Zhonghui. "Holding fast to vigor, how glorious"—this was how King Wu permanently cleared the Four Seas; yet that he did not treat the near with familiarity nor forget the distant was extolled by Meng Ke [Mencius]. Thus, Tang and Wu did not merely use martial force; rather, this was how they excelled in bringing their benevolence and wisdom to completion.

Descending from these eras, founding rulers who initiated the great enterprise to open the governance of an era, even though their virtue did not reach the realm of pure perfection, were nonetheless sufficient to bring about order. Thus, Emperor Gaozu of Han was generous, benevolent, and loving toward others, knowing men and excelling at employing them, and so in five years he accomplished the imperial enterprise; Emperor Guangwu of Han had brilliant court counsels and valiant, heroic decisiveness, and so in a few years he was able to achieve a dynastic restoration. One whose deeds compared to Tang and Wu and whose governance nearly matched Kings Cheng and Kang of Zhou was Emperor Taizong of Tang, and the Reign of贞观 (Zhenguan) ultimately founded the enterprise of the Tang house; one who was benevolent, filial, fraternal, intelligent, and magnanimous was Emperor Taizu of Song, and the grace of his benevolence and generosity ultimately bequeathed peace for several generations. Among these several sovereigns, some forged great enterprises through strictness and clarity, while others handed down vast blessings through loyalty and generosity; in their application of those three virtues, each indeed had what was fitting for him. As for rulers who preserved the achievements of their predecessors, succeeding to and guarding the ancestral enterprise to continue the succession of an era, even though their virtue did not reach the归宿 of pure refinement, they were nonetheless…

title: 萬曆十一年進士登科錄
text:
足以成治故漢文帝宋仁宗世所號爲仁主
也而富庶之風深仁之洽至今有遺美焉漢
明帝唐明皇世所稱爲睿主也而長厚之休
勵精之治至今有深羨焉漢武帝唐武宗世
所號爲英主也而雄邁之畧克敵之勳至今
猶可想焉之數君者或以柔道理天下或以
精勤致太平彼三德之用夫亦各有攸當也
籍令崇敦大之治於羣雄角逐之世則迂矣
厲鷹揚之烈於四方無虞之時則擾矣任苛
察之政於民風淳厚之俗則過矣狃因循之

punctuated:
足以成治。故漢文帝、宋仁宗，世所號爲仁主也，而富庶之風、深仁之洽，至今有遺美焉；漢明帝、唐明皇，世所稱爲睿主也，而長厚之休、勵精之治，至今有深羨焉；漢武帝、唐武宗，世所號爲英主也，而雄邁之畧、克敵之勳，至今猶可想焉。之數君者，或以柔道理天下，或以精勤致太平，彼三德之用，夫亦各有攸當也。籍令崇敦大之治於羣雄角逐之世，則迂矣；厲鷹揚之烈於四方無虞之時，則擾矣；任苛察之政於民風淳厚之俗，則過矣；狃因循之習於起敝扶衰之際，則隳矣。又何以開丕基而著鴻績，守成業而致盛治也哉！故匡衡疏六戒，而太察之與無斷，皆在所懲；陸贄陳九弊，而聰明之與威強，皆在所黜；蘇軾上六事，而兵刑之與智數，皆在所畧。數君子者，其各有見乎！
陛下臨御以來，十有一載於茲矣。勵精圖治，推心任人，固宜吏稱民安，政修事理，邊疆無桴鼓之警，方內無盜賊之憂，以彰
translation_en:
… suffice to achieve good governance. Thus Emperor Wen of Han (漢文帝) and Emperor Renzong of Song (宋仁宗) are hailed by the world as benevolent rulers; the ethos of wealth and populousness and the pervasiveness of their deep benevolence have left behind a beauty that endures to this day. Emperor Ming of Han (漢明帝) and Emperor Minghuang of Tang (唐明皇) are praised by the world as perspicacious rulers; the blessings of their generous kindness and the governance of their diligent vigor inspire deep admiration to this day. Emperor Wu of Han (漢武帝) and Emperor Wuzong of Tang (唐武宗) are hailed by the world as heroic rulers; their bold and surpassing strategies and their merits in vanquishing enemies can still be envisioned even today. Among these several sovereigns, some ordered the realm through gentle ways, while others brought about grand peace through dedicated diligence; in their application of those three virtues, each likewise had what was fitting for his circumstances. Suppose one were to exalt magnanimous and broad-minded governance in an age when rival warlords are contending for supremacy—that would be impractical! Or rouse hawk-like martial fierceness at a time when the four quarters are free from anxiety—that would cause disturbance! Or employ harsh and overly scrutinized administration among customs where the popular ethos is simple and honest—that would be excessive! Or cling to habits of passive routine at a juncture that calls for remedying decay and propping up decline—that would lead to ruin! How then could one lay down a great foundation and manifest grand achievements, or preserve an inherited patrimony and bring about flourishing governance? Therefore, when Kuang Heng (匡衡) memorialized on the six admonitions, both excessive scrutiny and indecisiveness were among the things to be guarded against; when Lu Zhi (陸贄) set forth the nine maladies, both reliance on personal cleverness and intimidating dominance were among the things to be rejected; and when Su Shi (蘇軾) presented the six matters, both military and penal affairs as well as calculating stratagems were among the things to be treated as secondary. Each of these several gentlemen surely had his own insight!
Since Your Majesty ascended the throne, eleven years have now passed. With diligent vigor You have sought good governance, and with sincere trust You have employed men; by rights it ought to be that officials are equal to their duties and the people are at peace, that administration is well-ordered and affairs are properly managed, that the frontiers have no alarms of war drums, and that within the realm there are no worries of bandits and thieves, so as to make manifest …

title: 萬曆十一年進士登科錄
text:
陛下平明之治可也乃者邇年以來紀綱屢飭而
吏無廉靜之風田野雖闢而民無康阜之化
學校常肅矣而青衿之士鮮氣節而寡廉耻
邊鄙雖寧矣而驕悍之卒辱主帥而逞姦謀
督捕雖嚴矣而潢池之赤子屢縱逸而拒威
命誠有如
聖制之所詢
宸衷之所慮者此何以致之也意者有司不能仰
體
德意而奉行之過乎臣愚以為吏之無良者旌别
===
未當也誠清入仕之途公銓選之法明黜陟
之等則奉法循理者益勵於為善貪墨不檢
者斂跡而不肆又何患乎吏治之不修民之
失業者催科太急也誠省賦斂之條緩積逋
之令寛力役之征則服田力穡者遂有秋之
望游惰無賴者樂耕耨之常又何患乎民生
之未遂學校者
國家養賢之所本以養賢而作新無術賢其可
興乎誠欲剛方正直之士接踵於朝博雅練
達之才不匱於用則廣厲學官而慎選明師

punctuated: 陛下平明之治可也。乃者邇年以來，紀綱屢飭，而吏無廉靜之風；田野雖闢，而民無康阜之化；學校常肅矣，而青衿之士鮮氣節而寡廉耻；邊鄙雖寧矣，而驕悍之卒辱主帥而逞姦謀；督捕雖嚴矣，而潢池之赤子屢縱逸而拒威命。誠有如聖制之所詢、宸衷之所慮者，此何以致之也？意者有司不能仰體德意，而奉行之過乎？臣愚以為，吏之無良者，旌别未當也。誠清入仕之途，公銓選之法，明黜陟之等，則奉法循理者益勵於為善，貪墨不檢者斂跡而不肆，又何患乎吏治之不修？民之失業者，催科太急也。誠省賦斂之條，緩積逋之令，寛力役之征，則服田力穡者遂有秋之望，游惰無賴者樂耕耨之常，又何患乎民生之未遂？學校者，國家養賢之所。本以養賢，而作新無術，賢其可興乎？誠欲剛方正直之士接踵於朝，博雅練達之才不匱於用，則廣厲學官，而慎選明師…
translation_en:
…Your Majesty's fair and enlightened governance. Yet in recent years, although laws and discipline have been repeatedly tightened, officials lack a spirit of integrity and quietude; although farmlands have been opened up, the common people enjoy no transformation toward peace and abundance; schools are regularly kept in solemn order, yet scholars in their blue collars rarely show moral courage and have little sense of honor or shame; although the frontier regions are tranquil, arrogant and unruly soldiers humiliate their commanding generals and carry out treacherous plots; although the supervision of arrests is strict, the Emperor's subjects who play with weapons in the ponds—the rebels and bandits—repeatedly escape and defy august commands. Truly, things are just as Your Sacred Decree has inquired and as the Imperial Mind has worried—how has this come about? Could it be that the authorities are unable to respectfully embody Your virtuous intentions, and have erred in carrying them out?

In Your Servant's humble opinion, that officials are unscrupulous is because the distinction between the good and the bad has not been properly made. If indeed the paths into officialdom are purified, the methods of personnel selection made impartial, and the grades of demotion and promotion clarified, then those who uphold the law and follow principle will be all the more encouraged to do good, while the corrupt and unrestrained will pull back and cease their excesses—what worry would there be that official administration is not put in order? That the common people lose their livelihoods is because the pressing for tax collection is too urgent. If indeed the articles of taxation are reduced, the orders for collecting accumulated arrears relaxed, and the levies of corvée labor made lenient, then those who toil in the fields and work hard at harvesting will fulfill their hopes for an autumn yield, and idle, shiftless vagrants will take joy in the regular routine of plowing and weeding—what worry would there be that the people's livelihood is not fulfilled? Schools are the places where the State nurtures the worthy. They are meant to nurture the worthy, yet if there is no method to rouse and renew them, how can the worthy rise up? If we truly wish for upright, square, and honest scholars to follow closely upon one another's heels at court, and for broadly learned, refined, and experienced talents never to be lacking for use, then we should broadly encourage the school officials and carefully select enlightened teachers…

title: 萬曆十一年進士登科錄
text:
可也軍士者
國家禦亂之資藉其禦亂而紀律不嚴軍其可
治乎誠欲三軍之士有投石超距之勇百萬
之師有搴旗陷陣之勳則時其訓練而倡其
勇敢可也盜賊之起而未息者由衣食之不
給也今不足其衣食而欲以刑驅之以勢格
之是趣其爲盜也無乃非計乎誠欲良民安
於爲善而姦民無以爲非郡縣無横行之夫
而長吏無盤詰之警則與以可生之途授以
爲善之資可也如是則綱紀畢張政事修理
===
時有所尚德緩刑而天下不得病其姑息時
有所發姦擿伏而天下不得病其煩苛時有
所用威克愛而天下不得病其亢暴將見四
海安瀾八荒效順又安有不升斯世於平康
而躋兆民於仁壽也哉然臣猶有所
獻焉臣聞君心者治之表也逸欲者亂之階也
君心一淆天下事無可爲者臣願
陛下懋德於深宫密勿之中而不間於
大廷
深慮夫百千萬世之遠而不忽於微眇

給也今不足其衣食而欲以刑驅之以勢格

而長吏無盤詰之警則與以可生之途授以

大廷
深慮夫百千萬世之遠而不忽於微眇
punctuated:
可也。軍士者，國家禦亂之資；藉其禦亂，而紀律不嚴，軍其可治乎？誠欲三軍之士有投石超距之勇，百萬之師有搴旗陷陣之勳，則時其訓練而倡其勇敢，可也。盜賊之起而未息者，由衣食之不給也；今不足其衣食，而欲以刑驅之、以勢格之，是趣其爲盜也，無乃非計乎？誠欲良民安於爲善，而姦民無以爲非，郡縣無横行之夫，而長吏無盤詰之警，則與以可生之途，授以爲善之資，可也。如是，則綱紀畢張，政事修理，時有所尚德緩刑，而天下不得病其姑息；時有所發姦擿伏，而天下不得病其煩苛；時有所用威克愛，而天下不得病其亢暴。將見四海安瀾，八荒效順，又安有不升斯世於平康，而躋兆民於仁壽也哉！

然臣猶有所獻焉。臣聞：君心者，治之表也；逸欲者，亂之階也。君心一淆，天下事無可爲者。臣願陛下懋德於深宫密勿之中，而不間於大廷；深慮夫百千萬世之遠，而不忽於微眇；
translation_en:
… will suffice. Soldiers are the state's resource for defending against disorder; if we rely on them to defend against disorder, yet discipline is not strict, how can the army be well governed? If we truly wish the men of the Three Armies to possess the valor to hurl stones and leap over barriers, and our hosts of a million to achieve the merit of capturing enemy standards and storming formations, then training them at the proper seasons and encouraging their bravery will suffice. That bandits and thieves arise and have not ceased is due to insufficiency of food and clothing; now, if we do not make their food and clothing sufficient, yet seek to drive them with punishments and restrain them by force, this is to hasten their becoming bandits—is it not a poor plan? If we truly wish good subjects to be content in doing good and wicked subjects to have no cause to do wrong, so that commanderies and counties have no lawless ruffians and chief local officials face no alarms requiring interrogation and inspection, then granting them a viable path to a livelihood and providing them with the means to do good will suffice. If it is done thus, the fundamental laws and discipline will be fully extended and governmental affairs will be ordered and regulated. At times there will be an emphasis on virtue and a relaxation of punishments, yet the empire will have no cause to fault it as indulgent laxity; at times there will be the exposure of wickedness and the uncovering of hidden crimes, yet the empire will have no cause to fault it as vexatious harshness; at times there will be the use of majesty to overcome affection, yet the empire will have no cause to fault it as overbearing tyranny. We shall see the Four Seas calm their waves and the Eight Wildernesses render obedience—how could we fail to raise this age to peace and tranquility, and lift the millions of people to benevolence and longevity!

Yet your servant still has something to offer. Your servant has heard that the ruler's mind is the standard of governance, while ease and desire are the stepping-stones to disorder. Once the ruler's mind is confused, nothing in the affairs of the empire can be accomplished. Your servant wishes Your Majesty to cultivate virtue in the secluded intimacy of the deep palace, without discrepancy in the Great Court; to ponder deeply the distant future of hundreds, thousands, and ten thousands of generations, without neglecting the minute and subtle; …

title: 萬曆十一年進士登科錄
text:
定計於碩德重望之臣而不惑於憸夫毋以治
平無事而縱逸樂毋以物力太盛而尚侈靡
毋以財用充盈而興土木毋以甘言悅己而
近嬖倖如是則
陛下之心澹然一無所好而衆欲之攻泊然一無
所投所謂仁明武之三德自然全體而不遺
時出而罔悖將直追夫唐虞三代之盛奚漢
宋之足云臣草茅之士不識忌諱干冒
宸嚴不勝戰慄隕越之至臣謹對

punctuated: 定計於碩德重望之臣，而不惑於憸夫。毋以治平無事而縱逸樂，毋以物力太盛而尚侈靡，毋以財用充盈而興土木，毋以甘言悅己而近嬖倖。如是，則陛下之心，澹然一無所好，而衆欲之攻，泊然一無所投。所謂仁、明、武之三德，自然全體而不遺，時出而罔悖，將直追夫唐、虞、三代之盛，奚漢、宋之足云！臣草茅之士，不識忌諱，干冒宸嚴，不勝戰慄隕越之至。臣謹對。
translation_en: …and settle Your plans with ministers of great virtue and weighty reputation without being misled by glib sycophants. Do not indulge in ease and pleasure because the realm is peaceful and untroubled; do not prize extravagance and luxury because material resources are exceedingly abundant; do not undertake construction works because finances and supplies are overflowing; do not draw close to favorites because sweet words please You. If You act thus, Your Majesty's mind will be tranquil and wholly free of cravings, and the assaults of myriad desires will find nowhere at all to lodge. What are called the three virtues of benevolence, perspicacity, and martial vigor will naturally be embodied in their entirety without omission, and brought forth at the proper time without perversion. You will directly rival the flourishing ages of Yao, Shun, and the Three Dynasties—what need is there even to mention Han and Song! Your servant is a rustic scholar who does not know what taboos to avoid; having offended the Imperial Majesty, I am overcome with trembling and the fear of disgracing myself. Your servant respectfully replies.

title: 萬曆十一年進士登科錄
text:
臣李廷機
臣對臣聞帝王之憲天而修德也必會乎其
全而後可以恢天下之治本必執乎其中而
後可以運天下之治機何謂全涵萬理聚衆
妙渾融合一而無乎弗備者是已何謂中順
時幾達變化斟酌劑量而無乎弗宜者是已
不會其全則得此而失彼得一而遺二不該
不徧德之一節也治本何由而恢不執其中
則流焉而不返亢焉而無制不冲不粹德之
一偏也治機何由而運夫惟聖帝明王卓乎
===
遠覽穆乎深思謂一節之德非德也而務會
其全舉吾德之所爲森然具者兼總而并包
之而不使天下得以議其闕謂一偏之德非
德也而務執其中舉吾德之所爲秩然宜者
化裁而時出之而不使天下得以議其過夫
既無所於闕而又無所於過則有該括天下
之全體而其敷施也弘有燮調天下之妙用
而其厝注也當自古明聖顯懿之主獨運密
勿之中而風行裨海之遠端拱堂皇之上而
化臻熈皡之隆者用此道而已矣晚近世之

臣李廷機
臣對臣聞帝王之憲天而修德也必會乎其
全而後可以㤥天下之治本必執乎其中而
後可以運天下之治機何謂全涵萬理聚衆
妙渾融合一而無乎弗備者是已何謂中順
時幾達變化斟酌劑量而無乎弗宜者是已
不會其全則得此而失彼得一而遺二不該
不徧德之一節也治本何由而㤥不執其中
則流焉而不返亢焉而無制不冲不粹德之
一偏也治機何由而運夫惟聖帝明王卓乎
===
遠覽穆乎深思謂一節之德非德也而務會
其全舉吾德之所為森然具者兼總而并包
之而不使天下得以議其闕謂一偏之德非
德也而務執其中舉吾德之所為秩然宜者
化裁而時出之而不使天下得以議其過夫
既無所於闕而又無所於過則有該括天下
之全體而其敷施也弘有爕調天下之妙用
而其曆注也當自古明聖顯懿之主獨運客
勿之中而風行裨海之遠端拱堂皇之上而
化臻熙皡之隆者用此道而已矣晚近世之
punctuated:
臣李廷機。
臣對：臣聞帝王之憲天而修德也，必會乎其全，而後可以恢天下之治本；必執乎其中，而後可以運天下之治機。何謂全？涵萬理，聚衆妙，渾融合一而無乎弗備者是已。何謂中？順時幾，達變化，斟酌劑量而無乎弗宜者是已。不會其全，則得此而失彼，得一而遺二，不該不徧，德之一節也，治本何由而恢？不執其中，則流焉而不返，亢焉而無制，不冲不粹，德之一偏也，治機何由而運？夫惟聖帝明王，卓乎遠覽，穆乎深思，謂一節之德非德也，而務會其全，舉吾德之所爲森然具者，兼總而并包之，而不使天下得以議其闕；謂一偏之德非德也，而務執其中，舉吾德之所爲秩然宜者，化裁而時出之，而不使天下得以議其過。夫既無所於闕，而又無所於過，則有該括天下之全體，而其敷施也弘；有燮調天下之妙用，而其厝注也當。自古明聖顯懿之主，獨運密勿之中，而風行裨海之遠，端拱堂皇之上，而化臻熈皡之隆者，用此道而已矣。晚近世之
translation_en:
Your servant Li Tingji 李廷機.
Your servant replies: Your servant has heard that when emperors and kings model themselves on Heaven and cultivate their virtue, they must first comprehend its entirety before they can expand the foundation of governance for all under Heaven; they must first hold fast to its mean before they can set in motion the pivot of governance for all under Heaven. What is meant by entirety? It is that which encompasses the myriad principles, gathers the multitude of subtleties, and blends them into a seamless unity with nothing left unprovided for. What is meant by the mean? It is that which accords with timelyincipiencies, comprehends transformations, and weighs and adjusts proportions so that nothing is inappropriate. If one does not comprehend its entirety, one grasps this while losing that, or attains one thing while omitting two; neither all-inclusive nor universal, this is merely a single facet of virtue—how then can the foundation of governance be expanded? If one does not hold fast to its mean, one drifts away without returning, or goes to extremes without restraint; neither harmonious nor pure, this is merely a one-sided virtue—how then can the pivot of governance be set in motion? Only the sage emperors and enlightened kings gaze afar with towering vision and ponder deeply in solemn contemplation. Holding that a single facet of virtue is not true virtue, they strive to comprehend its entirety, taking all that is richly present within our virtue, combining and encompassing it altogether, so as never to allow the world to criticize its deficiencies. Holding that a one-sided virtue is not true virtue, they strive to hold fast to its mean, taking all that is orderly and fitting within our virtue, tailoring it through transformation and bringing it forth at the proper time, so as never to allow the world to criticize its excesses. Now, when there is neither any deficiency nor any excess, one possesses the complete substance that encompasses all under Heaven, and its application is vast; one possesses the wondrous function that harmonizes all under Heaven, and its implementation is fitting. Since antiquity, bright, sagely, illustrious, and admirable rulers who wielded authority alone in the quiet of the inner court while their influence swept out to the distant seas, and who sat with folded hands in stately majesty high in the court while their transformative rule reached the pinnacle of serene and expansive prosperity, simply employed this Way and nothing more. Of late and recent ages, [rulers]…

title: 萬曆十一年進士登科錄
text:
主德既偏駁而非聖人之德則治亦卑陋而
非聖人之治此邃古之盛所以寥寥而追令
緒紹休風端有在於
今日也欽惟
皇帝陛下
躬上聖之資
履泰隆之運盖慨然有高世主之心焉
臨馭以來敬
天勤民合時幾而並勅
宵衣旰食勵臣鄰以交修天下之賢才已盡舉
===
用邪佞已盡屏除四海已盡無虞九夷八蠻
之在荒服之外者已盡賓貢治化之極真可
以六五帝而四三王矣乃猶
聖不自聖進臣等而策之于
廷諏以仁明武之德隲前王之遺軌究當世之
要務而戒臣等以勿諱也臣有以仰窺
陛下之心即無怠無荒之心好問好察之心矣臣
敢不披瀝以對臣聞帝王之道天道也帝王
之德天德也今夫天生成萬品甄陶羣類化
至弘矣顧沾濡滋潤則雨露布其澤炳燿照

陛下之心即無怠無荒之心好問好察之心矣臣

punctuated:
主，德既偏駁而非聖人之德，則治亦卑陋而非聖人之治。此邃古之盛所以寥寥，而追令緒、紹休風，端有在於今日也。欽惟皇帝陛下躬上聖之資，履泰隆之運，盖慨然有高世主之心焉。臨馭以來，敬天勤民，合時幾而並勅；宵衣旰食，勵臣鄰以交修。天下之賢才已盡舉用，邪佞已盡屏除，四海已盡無虞，九夷八蠻之在荒服之外者已盡賓貢。治化之極，真可以六五帝而四三王矣。乃猶聖不自聖，進臣等而策之于廷，諏以仁明武之德，隲前王之遺軌，究當世之要務，而戒臣等以勿諱也。臣有以仰窺陛下之心，即無怠無荒之心、好問好察之心矣。臣敢不披瀝以對？

臣聞帝王之道，天道也；帝王之德，天德也。今夫天生成萬品，甄陶羣類，化至弘矣。顧沾濡滋潤，則雨露布其澤；炳燿照
translation_en:
… rulers: since their virtue was one-sided and impure and not the virtue of the sages, their governance was likewise base and crude and not the governance of the sages. This is why the flourishing of remote antiquity has been so rarely matched, and why recovering that fine heritage and continuing those admirable customs rests squarely upon today. I reverently reflect that Your Majesty the Emperor, endowed in person with the qualities of the highest sage and treading in an era of great peace and prosperity, is moved with the aspiration to surpass the rulers of the age. Since ascending the throne to rule, You have revered Heaven and labored for the people, uniting every moment and subtle incipient tendency under vigilant command; dressing before dawn and eating after dusk, You have encouraged Your ministers and aides in mutual cultivation. The worthy talents of the empire have all been promoted and employed, the wicked and sycophantic have all been cast out, the Four Seas are wholly free from anxiety, and the Nine Yi and Eight Man tribes beyond the wild domains have all come in submission to present tribute. At this summit of transformative governance, You can truly make the Five Emperors six and the Three Kings four! Yet even in Your sagely perfection You do not regard Yourself as a sage: You have summoned Your servants to put policy questions to us in the court, inquiring into the virtues of benevolence, perspicacity, and martial vigor, assessing the traces left by former kings, investigating the urgent affairs of the present age, and admonishing Your servants to hold nothing back. Your servant is thus able to look up and discern Your Majesty's mind—it is none other than a mind free from idleness and negligence, a mind fond of questioning and examining. How could Your servant dare not pour out his heart in reply?

Your servant has heard that the Way of emperors and kings is the Way of Heaven, and the virtue of emperors and kings is the virtue of Heaven. Now Heaven gives birth to and completes the myriad things, molding and shaping all categories of beings; its transformative work is vast indeed. Yet for moistening and nourishing, rain and dew spread their beneficence; for shining brightly and illuminating…

title: 萬曆十一年進士登科錄
text:
臨則日月垂其光震動摧折則雷霆宣其威
之三者皆天德之所寄以流行於宇宙間其
總之也則相須而成化妙合而奏功不爲雨
露廢日月不爲日月廢雷霆亦不爲雷霆廢
雨露也而於是乎見天德之全其運之也則
節而不流止而不過雨露不以沾沾爲德日
月不以曒曒爲明雷霆亦不以轟轟然遶天
下而擊之爲威也而於是乎見天德之中然
則君德亦若是已爾夫天下方喁喁然待我
以生而吾乃操之以慘刻則膏澤不流而人
===
有莫必其命者矣天下方總總然待我以理
而吾乃居之以昏蔽則情僞弗照而人有得
遁其姦者矣天下方紛紛然待我以决而吾
乃當之以優柔則幾務弗斷而人有敢梗其
令者矣如此則天下幾何而治焉故孔子論
政推原於知仁勇之達德而司馬光歷事三
朝亦以仁明武爲獻誠見夫君德之要無以
易此也臣嘗見古記稱堯者曰其仁如天其
知如神稱舜者曰明物察倫由仁義行稱禹
者曰其仁可親其言可信何嘗言及武哉非

translation_en: …shining down, the sun and moon cast their light; for shaking and shattering, thunder and lightning proclaim their majesty. These three are all wherein Heaven's virtue resides, circulating throughout the universe. Taken together, they depend on one another to bring about transformation and wondrously combine to achieve results: the sun and moon are not dispensed with on account of rain and dew, thunder and lightning are not dispensed with on account of the sun and moon, nor are rain and dew dispensed with on account of thunder and lightning; and herein is seen the completeness of Heaven's virtue. In their operation, they are regulated without overflowing, and halt without going to excess: rain and dew do not make petty drenching their virtue, the sun and moon do not make harsh glare their clarity, nor do thunder and lightning make roaring across the world and striking it down their majesty; and herein is seen the centrality of Heaven's virtue. Such, then, is the virtue of the ruler as well, and nothing more. Now, when the world is looking up expectantly, waiting upon us for life, if we instead handle it with cruel severity, then nourishing grace will not flow, and people will have no assurance of their lives; when the world is gathered in multitudes, waiting upon us for order, if we instead preside over it in befuddled obscurity, then truth and falsehood will not be illuminated, and people will succeed in concealing their wickedness; when the world is in tangled confusion, waiting upon us for decision, if we instead meet it with weak indecisiveness, then critical affairs will not be resolved, and people will dare to obstruct our commands. If it is like this, how could the world ever be well governed? Therefore, when Confucius discussed governance, he traced its source to the universal virtues of wisdom, benevolence, and courage; and Sima Guang 司馬光, having served through three reigns, likewise presented benevolence, clarity, and martial decisiveness as his counsel, truly seeing that the essentials of a ruler's virtue cannot be exchanged for anything else. Your servant has observed that when ancient records praised Yao 堯, they said: "His benevolence was like Heaven, his wisdom like a spirit." When they praised Shun 舜, they said: "He was clear about things and scrutinized human relationships; he acted out of benevolence and righteousness." When they praised Yu 禹, they said: "His benevolence was approachable, his words trustworthy." When did they ever speak of martial decisiveness? It is not that…

title: 萬曆十一年進士登科錄
text:
無武也彼其世揖遜其俗渾噩武固無所用
之然而武未嘗不在其中也稱湯者曰天錫
勇知稱武者曰執競維烈何其專言武哉非
尚武也彼其世改革其俗漸染非武無以定
之然而仁明未嘗不在其中也何也仁明武
之德雖三而理則一帝王固一以貫之者也
不然四凶之誅防風之戮豈不武者之所能
而克寬克仁散財發粟又豈專尚武者之所
有哉晚近世之主闇於大道猥以一節自好
一偏自安是故論肇迹洪緒者亦有如漢高
===
之寬仁愛人知人善任矣如光武之明明廟
謨赳赳雄斷矣如唐宗之迹比湯武治幾成
康矣如宋祖之仁孝友愛聰明豁達矣然而
揆之三德則駁雜者多也即崛起一代開丕
丕之基而君子猶以為陋也論守成纘業者
亦有以仁稱如漢文帝宋仁宗矣有以明稱
如漢明帝唐明皇矣有以武稱如漢武帝唐
武宗矣然而責之三德則闕遺者多也即增
光宗祏享赫赫之名而君子猶以為愧也此
無他仁明武之德可兼而不可闕也故兼則

punctuated: 無武也。彼其世揖遜，其俗渾噩，武固無所用之，然而武未嘗不在其中也。稱湯者曰：「天錫勇知。」稱武者曰：「執競維烈。」何其專言武哉？非尚武也。彼其世改革，其俗漸染，非武無以定之，然而仁、明未嘗不在其中也。何也？仁、明、武之德雖三，而理則一，帝王固一以貫之者也。不然，四凶之誅、防風之戮，豈不武者之所能？而克寬克仁、散財發粟，又豈專尚武者之所有哉？晚近世之主，闇於大道，猥以一節自好，一偏自安。是故論肇迹洪緒者，亦有如漢高之寬仁愛人、知人善任矣；如光武之明明廟謨、赳赳雄斷矣；如唐宗之迹比湯、武，治幾成、康矣；如宋祖之仁孝友愛、聰明豁達矣。然而揆之三德，則駁雜者多也。即崛起一代，開丕丕之基，而君子猶以為陋也。論守成纘業者，亦有以仁稱，如漢文帝、宋仁宗矣；有以明稱，如漢明帝、唐明皇矣；有以武稱，如漢武帝、唐武宗矣。然而責之三德，則闕遺者多也。即增光宗祏，享赫赫之名，而君子猶以為愧也。此無他，仁、明、武之德，可兼而不可闕也。故兼則…
translation_en:
…that they lacked martial vigor. Rather, their ages were ones of yielding the throne, and their customs were simple and unadorned; there was inherently no occasion to employ martial vigor, and yet martial vigor was never absent from within. Those who praised Tang of Shang said: "Heaven endowed him with valor and wisdom." Those who praised King Wu of Zhou said: "Steadfast and strong, glorious was his achievement." Why did they speak so exclusively of martial vigor? It was not that they esteemed martial force alone. Rather, their ages were ones of dynastic revolution, and their customs had become tainted; without martial vigor there was no way to settle the realm, and yet benevolence and discernment were never absent from within. Why is this? Although the virtues of benevolence, discernment, and martial vigor are three, their underlying principle is one, and the emperors and kings of antiquity inherently bound them together as a single thread. Otherwise, how could the execution of the Four Criminals or the slaying of the lord of Fangfeng have been accomplished by someone lacking martial vigor? And how could the capacity for宽容 (magnanimity) and benevolence, or the dispersal of wealth and distribution of grain, have belonged to rulers who esteemed only martial force?

Rulers of later ages have been blind to the Great Way, basely indulging themselves in a single virtue and resting content with a one-sided partiality. Therefore, if we speak of those who founded dynasties and inaugurated great enterprises: there were indeed rulers like Gaozu of Han, who was magnanimous, benevolent, and loving toward others, and who knew men and employed them well; like Guangwu of Han, whose court counsels were brightly discerning and whose heroic decisiveness was martial and bold; like Taizong of Tang, whose deeds rivaled those of Tang and Wu and whose governance nearly matched that of Kings Cheng and Kang of Zhou; and like Taizu of Song, who was benevolent, filial, and fraternal, as well as intelligent and open-minded. Yet when we measure them against the three virtues, there was much that was impure and mixed. Even though they rose up to found an era and laid down a vast foundation, the superior man still regards them as deficient.

If we speak of those who preserved the accomplishments of their predecessors and carried on the dynastic enterprise: there were indeed those praised for benevolence, such as Emperor Wen of Han and Renzong of Song; those praised for discernment, such as Emperor Ming of Han and Emperor Xuanzong (Minghuang) of Tang; and those praised for martial vigor, such as Emperor Wu of Han and Wuzong of Tang. Yet when we hold them accountable to the three virtues, there was much that was lacking and omitted. Even though they added luster to their ancestral temples and enjoyed illustrious renown, the superior man still regards them as falling short. This is for no other reason than that the virtues of benevolence, discernment, and martial vigor must be combined and cannot be lacking in any part. Therefore, when they are combined…

title: 萬曆十一年進士登科錄
text:
治闕一則衰二則危司馬光所言詎非藎臣
之極思而哲王之炯戒哉若夫太察則苛矣
無斷則懦矣炫聰明則小矣厲威強則竭矣
喜兵刑則殘矣用智數則困矣之數者質之
德既不合施之治又不便此匡衡陸贄蘇軾
三臣者之所爲惓惓而慮切切而規也臣睹
古帝王之德之純其郅隆如彼世主之德之
衰其小康如此乃益知仁明武之德不可以
不全又不可以不中不全且中而能成至治
者自古及今未之嘗聞焉今
陛下以純天之心隆憲天之德
軫民窮布蠲恤即雨露之恩不渥於此矣
見萬里照覆盆即日月之明不炳於此矣斥邪
黨讋遠夷即雷霆之威不震於此矣蓋誠同
符天道媲美帝王而陋漢唐宋諸君於不足
道者固宜吏稱其職民安其業士飭于庠兵
輯于伍潢池無警外戶不扃而乃有少謬不
然者紀綱飭矣吏固多良矣而持祿養交後
公家之急者有之田野墾矣民固多粒矣而
藜藿不飽興仳離之嘆者有之學校肅矣士

治，闕一則衰，二則危。司馬光所言，詎非藎臣之極思，而哲王之炯戒哉？若夫太察則苛矣，無斷則懦矣，炫聰明則小矣，厲威強則竭矣，喜兵刑則殘矣，用智數則困矣。之數者，質之德既不合，施之治又不便，此匡衡、陸贄、蘇軾三臣者之所爲惓惓而慮、切切而規也。臣睹古帝王之德之純，其郅隆如彼；世主之德之衰，其小康如此。乃益知仁、明、武之德不可以不全，又不可以不中。不全且中而能成至治者，自古及今，未之嘗聞焉。
今陛下以純天之心，隆憲天之德。軫民窮，布蠲恤，即雨露之恩不渥於此矣；見萬里，照覆盆，即日月之明不炳於此矣；斥邪黨，讋遠夷，即雷霆之威不震於此矣。蓋誠同符天道，媲美帝王，而陋漢、唐、宋諸君於不足道者。固宜吏稱其職，民安其業，士飭于庠，兵輯于伍，潢池無警，外戶不扃。而乃有少謬不然者：紀綱飭矣，吏固多良矣，而持祿養交、後公家之急者有之；田野墾矣，民固多粒矣，而藜藿不飽、興仳離之嘆者有之；學校肅矣，士

…when all three are combined there is order; when one is lacking there is decline; when two are lacking there is peril. How could what Sima Guang 司馬光 said not be the deepest reflection of a loyal minister and a bright warning for a wise king? As for being overly scrutinizing, that is harshness; lacking decisiveness, that is weakness; flaunting cleverness, that is pettiness; straining ferocious might, that is exhaustion; delighting in warfare and punishments, that is cruelty; relying on manipulative stratagems, that is distress. Tested against virtue, these several tendencies do not accord with it, and applied to governance, they are disadvantageous. This is why those three ministers—Kuang Heng 匡衡, Lu Zhi 陸贄, and Su Shi 蘇軾—worried over them so earnestly and admonished against them so urgently. When your servant observes the purity of the virtue of the ancient emperors and kings, their supreme flourishing was like that; when I observe the decline of the virtue of later rulers, their lesser tranquility was like this. Thus I know all the more that the virtues of benevolence, discernment, and martial vigor must not fail to be complete, nor must they fail to hit the mean. That anyone from antiquity to the present has ever achieved ultimate order without these virtues being both complete and balanced—this has never been heard of.

Now Your Majesty, with a heart as pure as Heaven, exalts a virtue modeled on Heaven. You commiserate with the people's distress and promulgate tax remissions and relief—even the grace of rain and dew is no more abundant than this; you see ten thousand li away and illuminate beneath the overturned basin of injustice—even the brilliance of the sun and moon is no brighter than this; you expel perverse factions and overawe distant barbarians—even the majesty of thunderbolts is no more awe-inspiring than this. Truly you tally with the Way of Heaven, rival the excellence of the ancient emperors and kings, and look down upon the various rulers of the Han, Tang, and Song as unworthy of mention. It ought certainly to follow that officials fulfill their duties, the people rest secure in their livelihoods, scholars are disciplined in the schools, soldiers are harmonious in the ranks, there are no alarms of banditry, and outer doors need not be barred. And yet there are things slightly at odds with this: state discipline has been rectified and officials are indeed mostly good, yet there are those who cling to their stipends, cultivate personal connections, and put the urgent needs of the state last; the fields have been opened for cultivation and the people indeed mostly have grain, yet there are those who cannot get their fill even of coarse greens and raise sighs of separation and dispersal; the schools are solemn and scholars…

title: 萬曆十一年進士登科錄
text:
固多俊矣而棄薄行名出檢柙之外者有之
邊鄙寧矣行枚可弗事矣而士卒桀驁時逞
聚譁之逆督捕嚴矣柝鈴可漸徹矣而萑苻
出沒時恣剽奪之害如
聖問所慮即臣亦竊疑之乃臣愚則以為聖人之
所不能必者天下之治而所可盡者三德之
修德誠修即治效未臻不足以為患德誠未
修即治效可述猶足以為憂故堯舜三王不
問其咨而問四目四聰之未達不畏孔壬而
畏知人安民之未盡不憂商士而憂皇自敬
===
德之未能不恤頑民而恤所其無逸之未至
今
皇上仁已溥矣明已周矣當幾亦已斷矣而愚臣
之所惓惓者惟願
陛下不以為已足而益懋修焉夫仁非專事尚德
緩刑煦煦姑息之謂也明非專事發奸擿伏
屑屑煩苛之謂也武非專事威克厥愛猛然
亢暴之謂也其體欲全而其用欲中如是而
已矣臣願
陛下益修其全者以為天下恢治本仁足以育而
